title: Isabella I to the Duke of Estrada, Segovia 20 Aug 1503 (AGS PTR leg. 53 doc. 69; Bergenroth's S.E.T.c.I. L. 4 ff. 65-67), catalogue 287

documents.shelfmark: AGS, Patronato Real, leg. 53, doc. 69 (PARES 2207988), three ciphered copies X (f. 322), Y (f. 323), Z
documents.route: Isabella I (Segovia) -> Hernán Duque de Estrada, ambassador in England

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the images; the 3 Oct 1503 letter (PTR 53/72, clear copy) summarises its content

transcription.source: PARES images 1-4 and 7-8 of PTR 53/69 (988x1310 px), line strips at 4x
transcription.notes: Read into reading_X.md directly (codes with values, letter runs as plaintext, [..] for unread runs); no sign-level token file, so the length is not measured. About 480 code-group tokens counted in reading_X.md.

system.summary: Cifra general de los Reyes Católicos (Galende Díaz 1994): homophonic sign alphabet interleaved with two-to-four letter code groups (v-, x-, y-, z-, b-, c-).
system.sibling_key: Cifra general de los RRCC, the key of esp318 no. 92 (targets/esp318/keys/cifra_general.txt).
system.notes: entries 683 = code groups in Galende's plates. Bergenroth's 'two keys of cipher' is the code/letter mixture.

prior_solution.where: Bergenroth (CSP Spain i 369, 1862) could not decipher it; Tomokiyo suggested the Galende key but gave no reading; no edition found

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the problem with /goal (catalogue 287 text, 'find it on PARES, apply the Galende key'). No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: strips.py, halves.py, stack.py, zoom.py (line strips from PARES images)

solution.what: CSP Spain i 369 (BHO): Segovia 20 Aug 1503, 'two keys of cipher', not deciphered; Tomokiyo points to PTR 53/69 as a Galende-cipher letter.
PARES 2207985-2207991 (PTR 53/66-72) opened; first downloads all returned 53/72's images because PARES keys images to the last catalogo/show page of the session; refetched per record.
PTR 53/69 found to hold three ciphered copies of one letter (20 Aug, a September duplicate, 3 Oct 1503); Y dated Segovia xx de agosto, dorse 'Leg. 4 f. 65'.
Galende's Cifra general applied: first line reads 'Ya sabeys como el rey de Francia nos ronpio los dias passados la guerra en Napoles'.
Clear copy of the 3 Oct 1503 letter (PTR 53/72 f. 346) read; it summarises 'nuestras cartas de veinte de agosto' and gives vocabulary (afrontar, declarase, dos mil peones).
Copy X read line by line against Y and Z (reading_X.md): codes all consistent with the printed key; about half the letter-sign runs unreadable at 988 px.

Pushed for a fuller reading: all PARES image routes re-tested (max 997x1396, no IIIF); 4-6x sharpened strips read against Galende's sign plate. Isolated words gained; the open letter runs stay ambiguous.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): reading_X.md (codes with values, letter runs as read, [..] unread) and the partial sign transcription of copy Y ll. 1-10; no full sign-level transcription exists (PARES resolution)

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_X.md read through. Recto lines 1-11 and 14-15 build Spanish sentences; from line 12 to the end of the verso most lines are mostly [..], leaving half-phrases (9 of 82 sentences clean overall, docs/_check_reading.py). The texts entry split; the second part relabelled decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.5 -> ~0.23 (estimated, by lines).

PARES (AGS PTR 53/69, record 2207988) re-fetch attempted (research/reading_audit/b27_pares_fetch.py, curl): HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on every request, the site root included. No other reproduction online; DECODE has no record.

Copy X recto ll. 12-13, 16-46 and verso ll. 1-10 converted from reading_X.md to running text with code values (texts/PTR53-69_partial_reading.md; log texts/PTR53-69_reread_log.md); nothing added. Scored (b17_score.py, es): 0.128 clean (6/47). Kept decoded, not read.

v3 verification: the entry was scored on the whole of reading_X.md (0.358). Its read part, recto ll. 1-11 and 14-15, written out in PTR53-69_reading.md (research/reading_audit/v3a_estrada.py): 0.812 explicit-hole, plain 0.5. Keeps read.

outcome.method_basis: Galende's printed Cifra general de los Reyes Catolicos (Galende 1994), which Tomokiyo had named as the cipher of PTR 53/69 before the attempt, was applied unchanged to the three ciphered copies; the clear copy of the 3 Oct 1503 letter (PTR 53/72 f. 346) gave only sense and vocabulary.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: only text that builds sentences counts. Counted in lines of copy X (tokens per line not measured): 13 of its 57 lines (recto 1-11, 14-15) read; the rest is decoded, not read. About 0.23, estimated. The earlier 0.5 (share of cipher tokens with a value, estimated) is withdrawn as a reading figure. 23 Oct 2026 (b27): unchanged; the unread part (texts/PTR53-69_partial_reading.md) scores 0.128 clean and PARES could not be re-read (HTTP 429).

gaps.item: Letter-sign runs, about half the cipher tokens of each copy (154 [..] stretches in reading_X.md)
gaps.detail: PARES serves 988x1310 px; signs are 8-10 px high and the alphabet has several homophones per letter; three copies collated. Needs the AGS originals or a high-resolution reproduction.

gaps.item: Two later clear notes (X verso, Z recto foot)
gaps.detail: cursive notes at the same resolution, read in part

outcome.notes: Content recovered in outline: French war on Naples, Roussillon, Fuenterrabia, Guipuzcoa, Galicia; Henry VII bound by treaty to help; request for 2000 English foot. Not about the marriage. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the entry split; recto ll. 1-11 and 14-15 read, the rest relabelled decoded, not read.

texts.label: Isabella to the Duke of Estrada, Segovia, 20 Aug 1503: copy X recto ll. 1-11 and 14-15
texts.summary: Isabella tells Estrada that the King of France broke the peace in Naples without cause, has sent his power by sea and land to the frontiers of Roussillon and Fuenterrabía, and has opened war in Aragon, Guipúzcoa and Galicia; the King of England is bound by the treaties to help defend what is theirs, and Estrada is to ask for two thousand English foot with ships. About half of the letter-sign runs stay unread at the resolution PARES serves. reading_X.md gives code groups with their values and the letter runs as read; the sign-level transcription exists only for copy Y lines 1-10 (work_Y.md).

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored reading_X.md whole (all 46+11 lines, most unread, with code=value tags; 0.358). The read part the entry claims (recto ll. 1-11 and 14-15) written out in PTR53-69_reading.md (tags reduced to values, letter runs in lower case, supplied letters as holes, ll. 12-13 marked unread): 0.812 explicit-hole (13/16 sentences, hole rate 0.112); plain 0.5 (1503 spelling). Sentences hold except ll. 5-7 (several [..]).

texts.label: Isabella to the Duke of Estrada, Segovia, 20 Aug 1503: copy X recto ll. 12-13, 16-46 and verso
texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b27): no decipherment, copy or edition (the 3 Oct clear letter on PTR 53/72 only summarises it); the key (Galende's Cifra general) is complete, so the holes are unread signs. PARES answered HTTP 429 to every request on 23 Oct, so the images could not be re-read; on 22 Sept its maximum was 997 x 1396 px, where a sign is 8-10 px high. The unread lines converted to running text (texts/PTR53-69_partial_reading.md): 0.128 clean (6/47). Blocker: illegible at the only available resolution; better photographs of the three copies X, Y, Z need a request to AGS Simancas (needs-physical-access).
